Shoulder and arm trauma foundations: 1

A patient arrives with a deformed arm after a fall. Before splinting, the clinician records pulses, capillary refill, sensation and motor function, then repeats them afterward. Which assessment principle is being applied to this injury?

  1. CT to define the injury and adjacent structures
  2. Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment
  3. Protected early motion when stability permits
  4. Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture
  5. Document neurovascular status before and after intervention
Answer and explanation

Document neurovascular status before and after intervention

Serial motor, sensory and perfusion examinations establish baseline function and detect new deficits after reduction or splinting.

Option explanations

Document neurovascular status before and after intervention: Serial motor, sensory and perfusion examinations establish baseline function and detect new deficits after reduction or splinting.

CT to define the injury and adjacent structures: CT helps evaluate complex bony anatomy, articular involvement or sternoclavicular relationships when indicated. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment: Threatened neurovascular or mediastinal structures require urgent appropriately supported care, not casual manipulation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Protected early motion when stability permits: Appropriate early motion reduces stiffness; timing depends on stability and the treatment plan. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture: High-energy injuries can coexist with chest, neurovascular or adjacent-joint injuries that alter priorities. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
